beats.text: In the town of Emberhollow, third lantern past the fountain, there is a bookshop. It has stood since the Year of the Quiet Comet. Elves browse it for decades. Dwarves weep quietly in Poetry. Halflings leave crumbs in Cookery, and are forgiven, because they bring scones.

For twenty years it has been kept by Mirabel Thistlewick, who had it from her aunt. She knows every book on its shelves, and every patron by name. What she does not know, most evenings, is whether the shop made any money this month.

The ledger cannot tell her. Favourites run out. The queue runs out of the door. A bookwyrm is found asleep in Herbalism, very full, and not at all sorry. And last week, a signed first edition bit a knight. It was a mimic. So Pip, the clerk, ran to the tavern to find adventurers, and a price was agreed in a doorway. Nobody wrote it down.
The Scribes' Guild offered to help. A dozen scribes, a year and a day, and more gold than the shop takes in a decade.

So Mirabel sent for EPAM. They did not bring a dozen scribes. They brought a small team, and a scriptorium that never sleeps. One quill asks the questions she had not thought of. One draws up the plan. Several write at once. One reads every page back. And one carries the finished work to the shelf. The quills are tireless. The judgement is human.
Chapter one is already written. A shop front for the town. A counter for Mirabel and Pip. The catalog, the guest book, the incident board. It works. And now, Mirabel has a list.

At the top of it, in her own hand: For a dire incident, I want to post a bounty for adventurers. Today, you run the scriptorium, and you need not be an engineer to do it. First, together, the bounty board. After that, Mirabel's list is yours.
